<content>
1: # R196 — Theory Bottleneck Portfolio, Wave 1
2: 
3: Bu roundun hedefi bir ürünü seçmek değil, üç tarihî teorinin takıldığı işlemi
4: değiştirip yeni kabiliyet kalıp kalmadığını ölçmektir. Pozitif bir home-field
5: sonucu global teori çözümü veya novelty sayılmaz. Ham vakalar `R196_RESULT.json`,
6: çalışan deney `portfolio_wave1.py` içindedir.
7: 
8: ## Kısa hüküm
9: 
10: | Damar | Eski bottleneck | Yapısal değişiklik | Hüküm |
11: |---|---|---|---|
12: | Steinbuch Lernmatrix | Tek hit ile kalıcı hücre doygunluğu | Her hücreyi 2-bit yerel kanıta terfi; signed sınıf-dışı kanıt ablation'ı | Doygunluk kırıldı; signed kısmın eşit-bellek üstünlüğü kanıtlanmadı |
13: | Choquet capacity | Genel kapasitede `2^d-2` serbest değer | Sparse 2-additive Möbius support keşfi + closed-form exact monotonicity projection | Üstel bottleneck yalnız sparse 2-additive sınıfta kırıldı |
14: | Volterra hereditary series | İkinci mertebede `O(m^2)` kernel ve segmentler arası sahte hafıza | Rank-separable quadratic form + bilinen değişim sınırında hafıza reset | Deploy bottleneck'i düşük-rank sınıfta kırıldı; doğrudan faktör eğitimi açık |
15: 
16: ## HM-07 — Steinbuch: latch'ten küçük kanıt hücresine
17: 
18: 12 sınıf, 192 bit, üç load ve iki query-noise rejiminde 48 vaka çalıştı.
19: 
20: - Yüksek load'da binary latch matrisinin hücrelerinin `%82.48`i doldu ve accuracy
21:   `0.4533`e düştü.
22: - Signed ternary hücre `0.9992`, float centroid `0.9997`, aynı 2-bit unsigned
23:   count baseline'ı `0.9996` accuracy verdi.
24: - Signed ternary binary matrisi 40/48 vakada geçti; fakat aynı bellekli unsigned
25:   baseline'ı yalnız 4/48 vakada geçti.
26: 
27: Dolayısıyla **doygunluk sorunu çözülüyor**, ama güçlü fikir “signed evidence” diye
28: şişirilemez. Asıl terfi 1-bit irreversible memory'den küçük, yeniden ölçülebilir
29: evidence state'ine geçiştir. Bu şimdilik faydalı bir teori düzeltmesi; breakthrough
30: değildir.
31: 
32: ## HM-10 — Choquet: üstel capacity'den sparse interaction cebirine
33: 
34: 2-additive capacity şu şekilde yazıldı:
35: 
36: ```text
37: C_mu(x) = sum_i a_i x_i + sum_(i,j in E) b_ij min(x_i, x_j)
38: ```
39: 
40: Monotonicity'nin üstel subset taraması gerektirmeyen exact alt sınırı:
41: 
42: ```text
43: min_S Delta_i mu(S) = a_i + sum_(j: b_ij < 0) b_ij >= 0
44: ```
45: 
46: Bu eşitsizlik projection ve certificate olarak kullanıldı. 12/20 boyut, 80/200
47: örnek, 8 seed ile 32 sparse vakada:
48: 
49: - sparse model additive modeli 27/32;
50: - monotone full-pair modeli 32/32;
51: - monotonicity'siz raw full-pair modeli 32/32 geçti;
52: - 32/32 exact monotonicity certificate verdi;
53: - mean RMSE: additive `0.01644`, raw full pair `0.02150`, sparse `0.00688`;
54: - bulunan 7 interaction'ın ortalama `4.53`ü gerçek support'taydı.
55: 
56: Fakat dense-interaction stress'te full model 6/6 kazandı (`0.00145` vs `0.06574`).
57: Yani genel Choquet kapasitesinin üstel problemi çözülmedi; **sparse 2-additive
58: capacity sınıfı için** `O(d+s)` temsile ve exact certificate'e indirildi. Bir
59: sonraki ciddi adım support'un gerçekten sparse olup olmadığını veriden sertifika
60: eden bir testtir; aksi halde bu yöntem abstain etmelidir.
61: 
62: ## HM-12 — Volterra: yoğun hereditary kernelden separable memory'ye
63: 
64: İkinci mertebe kernel:
65: 
66: ```text
67: z^T H z  ->  sum_r lambda_r (v_r^T z)^2
68: ```
69: 
70: olarak terfi edildi. Bilinen segment/change sınırlarında lag state sıfırlandı;
71: önceki bağımsız rejimden sahte hafıza taşınmadı. 16 memory, rank 3, iki train
72: load'u ve 8 seed ile 16 vakada:
73: 
74: - separable model dense Volterra'nın %10 bandında 16/16 kaldı ve ortalamada daha
75:   düşük RMSE verdi (`0.01826` vs `0.02197`);
76: - linear modeli 16/16 geçti (`0.56187` mean RMSE);
77: - boundary-aware sürüm no-reset sürümü 16/16 geçti (`0.01826` vs `0.30429`);
78: - deploy parametreleri 152'den 67'ye, `%55.9` azaldı.
79: 
80: Dense-rank stress'te sonuç tersine döndü: dense model 6/6 kazandı (`0.01333` vs
81: `0.46308`). Ayrıca mevcut deney önce dense `H` fit edip sonra rank-truncate ediyor.
82: Bu nedenle **deploy/kernel representation bottleneck'i** low-rank ve boundary
83: marker bulunan sınıfta kırıldı; training bottleneck'i ancak faktörleri dense
84: matris kurmadan doğrudan öğrenirsek kırılmış olacak.
85: 
86: ## Disruption okuması — şimdilik yalnız kabiliyet
87: 
88: - Steinbuch hattı disruption adayı değil; basit ama sağlam bir düzeltme.
89: - Choquet hattındaki ilginç kabiliyet, az sayıda signed interaction ile karar
90:   fonksiyonunu hem compact hem exact monotone tutabilmek. Önce sparsity-abstention
91:   çözülmeli.
92: - Volterra hattındaki ilginç kabiliyet, nonlinear uzun hafızayı dense kernel
93:   taşımadan çalıştırmak. Doğrudan online factor learning çözülürse gerçek bir
94:   teori ilerlemesine dönüşebilir.
95: 
96: Bu yorumlar ürün seçimi değildir. Bir sonraki wave teorik açık işlemleri hedefler:
97: Pugachev'de conditional expectation/closure, Aizerman'da support growth ve
98: Glushkov'da composition state explosion.
99: 
100: ## Kaynak sınırı
101: 
102: - Steinbuch, *Die Lernmatrix*, Kybernetik 1 (1961), 36–45:
103:   https://bibbase.org/network/publication/steinbuch-dielernmatrix-1961
104: - Choquet, *Theory of capacities* (1954):
105:   https://www.numdam.org/articles/10.5802/aif.53/
106: - Volterra'nın integral-equation/functional hattındaki birincil kitaplarından
107:   *The theory of permutable functions* (1915) taraması:
108:   https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:The_theory_of_permutable_functions_(IA_theoryofpermutab00voltrich).pdf
109: 
110: Low-rank Volterra ve sparse/k-additive Choquet modern prior-art alanlarıdır.
111: Buradaki deneyler novelty değil, bottleneck hükmü verir; collision audit açıktır.

1: # R205 — Tarihî darboğazlar için nötr teori dalgası
2: 
3: ## Amaç ve sınır
4: 
5: Bu not bir ürün belgesi, akademik makale taklidi veya tek bir nişe doğru yol
6: haritası değildir. Altı tarihî araştırma hattında daha önce açık kalmış altı
7: farklı işlemi ele alır. Hedef, tarihî metni olduğu gibi yeniden uygulamak değil,
8: o metnin ulaşamadığı kabiliyeti bugün hangi ek varsayım veya yeni temsil ile
9: elde edebildiğimizi açıkça göstermektir.
10: 
11: Her bölüm şu ayrımı korur:
12: 
13: - **çözülen:** verilen varsayımlar altında yeni sonuç;
14: - **çözülmeyen:** varsayım kaldırıldığında açık kalan problem;
15: - **yenilik durumu:** burada ispatlanan şeyin doğru olması, literatürde ilk kez
16:   burada bulunduğu anlamına gelmez. Ayrıntılı collision audit daha sonra yapılır.
17: 
18: Pugaçev hattı R204'te ikinci tur survivor olarak park edilmiştir. Bu not, o tek
19: koordinatı daha fazla kazmak yerine araştırma genişliğini geri getirir.
20: 
21: ---
22: 
23: ## 1. Markov hattı: bilinmeyen thinning oranını deney tasarımıyla tanımlamak
24: 
25: ### Eski açık işlem
26: 
27: Birinci-mertebe zincirin gerçek geçiş matrisi `P` olsun. Her gerçek olay bağımsız
28: olarak `p=1-r` olasılıkla kaydedilirse retained olaylar arasındaki population
29: geçişi
30: 
31: \[
32: Q_p=pP\bigl[I-(1-p)P\bigr]^{-1}
33: \]
34: 
35: olur. `p` biliniyorsa `P` explicit olarak geri alınabilir. Yalnız `Q_p`
36: gözleniyorsa ise `p` genel olarak tanımlanamaz: farklı `p` değerleri farklı `P`
37: matrisleriyle aynı gözlenen zinciri verebilir.
38: 
39: Buradaki değiştirme, daha karmaşık bir estimator kurmak değil, **gözlem
40: düzenini** değiştirmektir. Aynı bilinmeyen retention işlemi iki kez ardışık
41: uygulansın:
42: 
43: - logger 1 gerçek zinciri `p` ile tutar ve `Q_p` üretir;
44: - logger 2 logger 1'in tuttuğu olayları yine aynı `p` ile tutar ve toplamda
45:   `Q_{p^2}` üretir.
46: 
47: ### Önerme 1 — nested-thinning tanımlanabilirliği
48: 
49: `P`, `Q_p` ve `Q_{p^2}` tersinir; `P != I`; `0<p<=1` olsun. Şu dönüşümü
50: tanımlayalım:
51: 
52: \[
53: \mathcal A(X)=X^{-1}-I.
54: \]
55: 
56: O zaman
57: 
58: \[
59: \mathcal A(Q_p)=\frac1p\mathcal A(P),
60: \qquad
61: \mathcal A(Q_{p^2})=\frac1{p^2}\mathcal A(P),
62: \]
63: 
64: ve dolayısıyla
65: 
66: \[
67: \mathcal A(Q_{p^2})=\frac1p\mathcal A(Q_p).
68: \]
69: 
70: Population seviyesinde bilinmeyen retention doğrudan
71: 
72: \[
73: \boxed{
74: p=
75: \frac{\langle \mathcal A(Q_p),\mathcal A(Q_p)\rangle_F}
76:      {\langle \mathcal A(Q_{p^2}),\mathcal A(Q_p)\rangle_F}
77: }
78: \]
79: 
80: ile, gerçek zincir ise
81: 
82: \[
83: \boxed{P=\bigl[I+p\mathcal A(Q_p)\bigr]^{-1}}
84: \]
85: 
86: ile belirlenir.
87: 
88: ### İspat
89: 
90: Tanımdan
91: 
92: \[
93: Q_p^{-1}
94: =\frac1p\bigl[I-(1-p)P\bigr]P^{-1}
95: =\frac1pP^{-1}-\frac{1-p}{p}I.
96: \]
97: 
98: Her iki taraftan `I` çıkarınca
99: 
100: \[
101: Q_p^{-1}-I=\frac1p(P^{-1}-I)
102: \]
103: 
104: elde edilir. Aynı eşitliği `p^2` için yazmak proportionality sonucunu verir.
105: `P!=I` olduğu için `A(Q_p)` sıfır değildir; Frobenius iç çarpımı scalar `p`yi
106: verir. Son eşitliği `P` için çözmek ikinci kutulu formülü verir. ∎
107: 
108: ### Neyi çözüyor?
109: 
110: Tek retained sequence'te çözülemeyen retention-rate tanımlanabilirliği, aynı
111: sampling işleminin kontrollü biçimde iki kez uygulanabildiği durumda optimizer,
112: EM veya zaman damgası olmadan çözülür. Ek bilgi bir prior değil, ikinci bir
113: gözlem operatörüdür.
114: 
115: Finite sample'da iki `A` matrisinin proportionality residual'ı aynı zamanda
116: model kontrolüdür:
117: 
118: \[
119: \rho=\min_{c>0}
120: \frac{\|\mathcal A(\widehat Q_{p^2})-c\mathcal A(\widehat Q_p)\|_F}
121:      {\|\mathcal A(\widehat Q_{p^2})\|_F}.
122: \]
123: 
124: `rho` büyükse homogeneous Markov, bağımsız thinning veya eşit-retention
125: varsayımlarından en az biri bozulmuştur; inversion abstain etmelidir.
126: 
127: ### Açık sınır
128: 
129: - Singular `P` için ters yerine invariant-subspace/resolvent formu gerekir.
130: - İkinci logger'ın retention'ı birincisiyle aynı değil ve aralarındaki ilişki

1: from __future__ import annotations

8: def thinned_transition(transition: np.ndarray, retention: float):
9:     identity = np.eye(len(transition))
10:     return (
11:         retention
12:         * transition
13:         @ np.linalg.inv(identity - (1.0 - retention) * transition)
14:     )

17: def recover_nested_thinning(first: np.ndarray, second: np.ndarray):
18:     identity = np.eye(len(first))
19:     first_transform = np.linalg.inv(first) - identity
20:     second_transform = np.linalg.inv(second) - identity
21:     retention = float(
22:         np.sum(first_transform * first_transform)
23:         / np.sum(second_transform * first_transform)
24:     )
25:     transition = np.linalg.inv(identity + retention * first_transform)
26:     return retention, transition

29: def preisach_prefix_output(weights: np.ndarray, frontier: np.ndarray):
30:     prefix = np.cumsum(weights, axis=1)
31:     active = frontier >= 0
32:     return float(
33:         np.sum(prefix[np.arange(len(frontier))[active], frontier[active]])
34:     )

37: def preisach_dense_output(weights: np.ndarray, frontier: np.ndarray):
38:     state = np.zeros_like(weights)
39:     for row, stop in enumerate(frontier):
40:         if stop >= 0:
41:             state[row, : stop + 1] = 1.0
42:     return float(np.sum(weights * state))

45: def recover_symmetric_low_rank(matrix: np.ndarray, probe_count: int, seed: int = 0):
46:     dimension = len(matrix)
47:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
48:     probes = rng.normal(size=(dimension, probe_count))
49: 
50:     def quadratic(vector):
51:         return float(vector @ matrix @ vector)
52: 
53:     def bilinear(left, right):
54:         return (quadratic(left + right) - quadratic(left - right)) / 4.0
55: 
56:     image = np.empty((dimension, probe_count))
57:     identity = np.eye(dimension)
58:     for row in range(dimension):
59:         for column in range(probe_count):
60:             image[row, column] = bilinear(identity[row], probes[:, column])
61:     basis, _ = np.linalg.qr(image)
62:     basis = basis[:, :probe_count]
63:     core = np.empty((probe_count, probe_count))
64:     for row in range(probe_count):
65:         for column in range(probe_count):
66:             core[row, column] = bilinear(basis[:, row], basis[:, column])
67:     return basis @ core @ basis.T

83:     }
84:     states = [
85:         np.array([1, 0], dtype=int),
86:         np.array([0, 1], dtype=int),
87:         np.array([1, 0], dtype=int),
88:     ]
89:     outputs = [
90:         np.array([1, 2], dtype=int),
91:         np.array([2, 1], dtype=int),
92:         np.array([1, 3], dtype=int),
93:     ]
94:     lifted = np.concatenate([states[0], np.kron(states[1], states[2])])
95:     lifted_output = np.concatenate(
96:         [outputs[0], 2 * np.kron(outputs[1], outputs[2])]
97:     )
98:     for symbol in word:
99:         blocks = transitions[symbol]
100:         states = [blocks[index] @ states[index] % modulus for index in range(3)]
101:         lifted_transition = np.zeros((6, 6), dtype=int)
102:         lifted_transition[:2, :2] = blocks[0]
103:         lifted_transition[2:, 2:] = np.kron(blocks[1], blocks[2])
104:         lifted = lifted_transition @ lifted % modulus
105:     direct = int(
106:         (
107:             outputs[0] @ states[0]
108:             + 2 * (outputs[1] @ states[1]) * (outputs[2] @ states[2])
109:         )
110:         % modulus
111:     )
112:     represented = int(lifted_output @ lifted % modulus)
113:     return direct, represented
114: 
115: 
116: def reduce_convex(points: np.ndarray, weights: np.ndarray, tolerance: float = 1e-11):
117:     points = points.copy()
118:     weights = weights.copy()
119:     dimension = points.shape[1]
120:     while len(weights) > dimension + 1:
121:         augmented = np.vstack([points.T, np.ones(len(points))])
122:         _, _, right = np.linalg.svd(augmented, full_matrices=True)
123:         dependence = right[-1]
124:         positive = dependence > tolerance
125:         if not np.any(positive):
126:             dependence = -dependence
127:             positive = dependence > tolerance
128:         ratio = np.full(len(weights), np.inf)
129:         ratio[positive] = weights[positive] / dependence[positive]
130:         drop = int(np.argmin(ratio))
131:         step = ratio[drop]
132:         weights = weights - step * dependence
133:         # In exact arithmetic the selected coefficient is zero.  Delete that
134:         # index explicitly so floating-point residue cannot stall the
135:         # constructive Caratheodory reduction.
136:         points = np.delete(points, drop, axis=0)
137:         weights = np.delete(weights, drop)
138:         weights = np.maximum(weights, 0.0)
139:         weights /= np.sum(weights)
140:     return points, weights
141: 
142: 
143: def compress_signed_responses(responses: np.ndarray, coefficients: np.ndarray):
144:     compressed = []
145:     for sign in (1.0, -1.0):
146:         selected = coefficients * sign > 0.0
147:         mass = float(np.sum(np.abs(coefficients[selected])))
148:         if not mass:
149:             continue
150:         points, weights = reduce_convex(
151:             responses[selected], np.abs(coefficients[selected]) / mass
152:         )
153:         compressed.append((sign, mass, points, weights))
154:     return compressed
155: 
156: 
157: def compressed_response(compressed):
158:     if not compressed:
159:         return np.array([])
160:     result = np.zeros(compressed[0][2].shape[1])
161:     for sign, mass, points, weights in compressed:
162:         result += sign * mass * (weights @ points)
163:     return result
164: 
165: 
166: def two_color_core_is_unsatisfiable(edges):
167:     vertices = sorted(set(itertools.chain.from_iterable(edges)))
168:     for colors in itertools.product((0, 1), repeat=len(vertices)):
169:         assignment = dict(zip(vertices, colors))
170:         if all(assignment[left] != assignment[right] for left, right in edges):
171:             return False
172:     return True
173: 
174: 
175: def permute_edges(edges, permutation):
176:     return [tuple(sorted((permutation[left], permutation[right]))) for left, right in edges]

305: ## 4. Volterra hattı: dense kernel kurmadan doğrudan rank-`r` tanımlama
306: 
307: ### Eski açık işlem
308: 
309: R196, quadratic Volterra kernel'ini dense `H` fit ettikten sonra rank-truncate
310: etti. Deploy ucuzladı fakat training hâlâ `O(m^2)` kernel'i kurdu. Açık problem,
311: factor'ları dense matrise hiç uğramadan tanımlamaktır.
312: 
313: Burada passive regression yerine tarihî sistem-identification ruhuna daha uygun
314: bir ek kabiliyet kullanılır: resetlenebilir sistem ve aktif probe input'ları.
315: 
316: İkinci derece response
317: 
318: \[
319: y(z)=b+\ell^Tz+z^THz,
320: \qquad H=H^T,quad \operatorname{rank}(H)=r
321: \]
322: 
323: olsun. `z`, bir deneyde hazırlanan lag/input-history vector'üdür.
324: 
325: Önce odd ve constant parçaları symmetric probing ile kaldır:
326: 
327: \[
328: q(z)=\frac{y(z)+y(-z)-2y(0)}2=z^THz.
329: \]
330: 
331: Polarization ile bilinear oracle elde edilir:
332: 
333: \[
334: \mathcal B(u,v)=\frac{q(u+v)-q(u-v)}4=u^THv.
335: \]
336: 
337: ### Önerme 4 — active low-rank Volterra recovery
338: 
339: `Omega in R^{m x s}` sürekli bir dağılımdan seçilsin ve `s>=r` olsun. Şu matrisi
340: bilinear probe'larla kur:
341: 
342: \[
343: Y=H\Omega,
344: \qquad Y_{ij}=\mathcal B(e_i,\omega_j).
345: \]
346: 
347: Olasılık 1 ile `range(Y)=range(H)` olur. `U=orth(Y)` ve
348: 
349: \[
350: M_{ab}=\mathcal B(u_a,u_b)
351: \]
352: 
353: seçilirse
354: 
355: \[
356: \boxed{H=UMU^T}
357: \]
358: 
359: exact'tır. Gerekli bilinear sorgu sayısı `ms+r^2`; `s=r` ile
360: `O(mr+r^2)` olur ve dense `m^2` kernel hiç kurulmaz.
361: 
362: ### İspat
363: 
364: Symmetric rank-`r` matris için `H=U_* Lambda U_*^T` yazılabilir. O zaman
365: 
366: \[
367: Y=U_*\Lambda(U_*^T\Omega).
368: \]
369: 
370: Random `Omega` için `U_*^T Omega` satır-rank `r` olur; dolayısıyla
371: `range(Y)=range(U_*)=range(H)`. `U` aynı range'in ortonormal basis'idir ve
372: `H=UU^THUU^T`. Orta blok `U^THU` tam olarak bilinear probe'lardan gelen `M`dir.
373: ∎
374: 
375: ### Neyi çözüyor?
376: 
377: Quadratic, symmetric, düşük-rank ve aktif olarak probe edilebilen Volterra
378: sisteminde direct factor identification problemi çözülür. Çözüm nonconvex factor
379: optimization yapmaz; önce range'i bulur, sonra yalnız `r x r` core'u ölçer.
380: 
381: ### Açık sınır
382: 
383: - Passive tek trajectory'de gereken probe vector'ları üretilemeyebilir.
384: - Reset yoksa lag histories birbirine karışır.
385: - Noise altında exact rank yerine randomized numerical-rank ve confidence
386:   analizi gerekir.
387: - Higher-order Volterra tensorleri için bilinear polarization yeterli değildir.
388: 
389: **Hüküm:** R196'nın “direct factor training açık” problemi aktif-identification
390: sınıfında teorik olarak kapanır; passive genel problem açık kalır.
391: 
392: ---
393:

395:

1: # LabAllCompass project contract
2: 
3: This repository is a research-and-product laboratory. The main loop is practical: inspect existing products/results/code/tests and R/T/IM memory, search broadly when useful, build or combine a promising mechanism, run the cheapest discriminating code/test, keep what works, record what fails, and move to the next product/problem.
4: 
5: ## Core boundaries
6: 
7: - R### research rounds, T## reusable mechanisms, IM-### primitives, products, tests and negative results remain useful Lab memory.
8: - A local failure does not globally kill a mechanism.
9: - Contracts and provenance may record useful facts, but they must not choose the research direction or become prerequisites for ordinary exploration, coding or testing.
10: - Do not treat document reading, gate completion, receipts, hashes or metadata as scientific progress by themselves.
11: - Coherence OS is memory/catalog/integrity through the active history. It may help find prior work, contradictions and failures, but it does not choose research direction or impose a stage order.
12: - Lab Runtime is optional persistence/execution journaling. Its routes are suggestions, not scientific gates.
13: - `POST_R178_SALVAGE_ARCHIVE/` preserves discarded R179-R192 code/mechanics only. Never auto-load, retrieve, rank, compose or cite it during normal Lab work; a salvaged mechanic may return only through a fresh experiment and a new identity.
14: - Active Turing history ends at R178. The next clean round is R179; R179-R192 from the discarded branch are not active Lab history.
15: 
16: ## Working style
17: 
18: Start from an interesting problem, product weakness, historical clue, mechanism, or promising combination. Use Lab products and R/T/IM memory as tools, not gates. Search external material according to the problem. Prefer code, tests, benchmarks, counterexamples and measurable improvements. When a path is weak, record the failure and move on.

</content>

Sorry — my last few replies came out garbled. Here's the whole assessment, once, cleanly:

**The idea (R205, Prop 4):** for a quadratic Volterra response with symmetric rank-`r` kernel, reset-and-probe access gives a bilinear oracle via polarization; `s ≥ r` random probes identify `range(H)`, `r²` more give the core, and `H = UMUᵀ` is recovered exactly in `O(mr + r²)` — the dense `m²` kernel is never formed.

**Why it's promising for agents:** an agent's history is a lag state carried densely (full transcripts, attention over everything). This reframes agent memory as an *identification* problem, not a compression problem: if the memory a policy actually uses is low-rank, you can discover it by re-rolling episodes with perturbed inputs and carry `r` factors + an `r×r` core instead of the whole transcript. Reset-and-probe is native to agents (re-roll, vary one input, diff behavior — basically how you debug them already), and R196's boundary-reset maps to task boundaries, killing exactly the spurious cross-task carry-over that plagues long agent sessions.

**Honest caveats:**
- Agent probes are noisy stochastic rollouts, not exact oracles → you'd need the randomized numerical-rank + confidence variant the note itself flags as open (line 385–386).
- Real memory isn't symmetric or exactly quadratic — it's an assumption to test empirically, and the natural experiment is: fit the low-rank model from probes, then predict held-out episode behavior vs. a dense baseline.
- Higher-order interactions need tensor polarization — a real extension, not a freebie.

**My verdict:** as an agent-memory mechanism it's a credible research direction, not a proven one — the theory is exact, the transfer to noisy rollout data is the actual open problem. The cheapest discriminating next step (in the lab's own spirit): instrument a small agent task, probe with reset-replays, and measure whether effective rank `r` stays small and held-out prediction beats a dense baseline. I can help set that experiment up — want me to?

## Derivation / assumptions
Response `y(z)=b+ℓᵀz+zᵀHz`, `H=Hᵀ, rank r`, resettable replay with i.i.d. noise. Four-point polarization `B(u,v)=(ȳ(u+v)+ȳ(−u−v)−ȳ(u−v)−ȳ(−u+v))/8 = uᵀHv` (Var `σ²/(16n)`); `Y=B(e_i,ω_j)=HΩ+ε` so `range(Y)=range(H)` a.s. for `s≥r`; learner stores `U (m×k)` + core `M (k×k)`, never dense `H`. ## Limitations
Dense baseline budget not equalized (active learner gets extra probe replays — explicit non-equivalence, stated in README); rank selection weak under noise, honestly reported via `abstain_rate`; synthetic quadratic oracle is **not** evidence agents have quadratic low-rank sufficient state (histories ≠ vector lag states; sum/negative probes ≠ text histories; static recovery ≠ recurrent sufficiency — stated in README); higher-order Volterra tensors out of scope.

10: def make_ground_truth(m, r, condition, rng):
11:     radii = np.geomspace(1.0, 1.0 / condition, num=r)
12:     signs = rng.choice([-1.0, 1.0, 1.0], size=r)
13:     v, _ = np.linalg.qr(rng.normal(size=(m, r)))
14:     h = (v * (radii * signs)) @ v.T
15:     offset = rng.normal()
16:     linear = rng.normal(size=m)
17:     return h, offset, linear
18:

20: def build_runner(h, offset, linear, noise_sigma, rng):
21:     def response(z, n):
22:         z = np.asarray(z, dtype=float)
23:         single = z.ndim == 1
24:         if single:
25:             z = z[None, :]
26:         mean = offset + z @ linear + np.einsum("ij,jk,ik->i", z, h, z)
27:         mean = np.broadcast_to(mean, (n, len(z)))
28:         sample = mean + noise_sigma * rng.normal(size=(n, len(z)))
29:         if single:
30:             return sample[0]
31:         return sample
32: 
33:     return response

36: def noiseless_bilinear(response, u, v, n):
37:     u = np.asarray(u, dtype=float)
38:     v = np.asarray(v, dtype=float)
39:     plus = float(np.mean(response(u + v, n)))
40:     minus = float(np.mean(response(-u - v, n)))
41:     cross = float(np.mean(response(u - v, n))) + float(
42:         np.mean(response(-u + v, n))
43:     )
44:     return (plus + minus - cross) / 8.0

46:

50:     image = np.empty((m, s))
51:     for i in range(m):
52:         for j in range(s):
53:             image[i, j] = noiseless_bilinear(
54:                 response, identity[i], omega[:, j], n
55:             )
56:     return image

59: def random_omega(m, s, rng):

117:     offset = float(np.mean(response(np.zeros(m), n)))
118:     u_cal_full = np.linalg.svd(image[:, calibration_idx], full_matrices=False)[0]
119:     scores = {}
120:     for rank in rank_grid:
121:         rank = int(rank)
122:         if rank < 1 or rank > len(calibration_idx) or rank > m:
123:             continue
124:         u_cal = u_cal_full[:, :rank]
125:         core_cal = probe_core(response, u_cal, n)
126:         kernel_cal = u_cal @ core_cal @ u_cal.T
127:         errors = []
128:         for _ in range(validation_count):
129:             z = rng.normal(size=m)
130:             target = mean_target(response, z, n)
131:             prediction = float(z @ kernel_cal @ z) + offset
132:             errors.append((prediction - target) ** 2)
133:         scores[rank] = float(np.mean(errors))
134:     if not scores:
135:         return 1, image, scores
136:     best_rank = min(scores, key=scores.get)
137:     return best_rank, image, scores
138: 
139: 
140: def mean_target(response, z, n):
141:     target = response(z, n)
142:     return float(np.mean(target))
143: 
144: 
145: def evaluate_kernel(kernel, z_set, n, response):
146:     errors = []
147:     offset = float(np.mean(response(np.zeros(len(z_set[0])), n)))
148:     for z in z_set:
149:         target = mean_target(response, z, n)
150:         prediction = float(z @ kernel @ z) + offset
151:         errors.append((prediction - target) ** 2)
152:     return float(np.mean(errors)), float(np.std(errors))
153: 
154: 
155: def dense_features(z):
156:     outer = np.outer(z, z)
157:     return np.concatenate([[1.0], z, outer[np.triu_indices(len(z))]])
158: 
159: 
160: def dense_feature_matrix(z_set):
161:     return np.vstack([dense_features(np.asarray(z)) for z in z_set])
162: 
163: 
164: def ridge_fit(features, targets, ridge):
165:     gram = features.T @ features + ridge * np.eye(features.shape[1])
166:     weights = np.linalg.solve(gram, features.T @ targets)
167:     return weights
168: 
169: 
170: def collect_targets(response, z_set, n):
171:     return np.array([mean_target(response, z, n) for z in z_set])
172: 
173: 
174: def fit_dense_baseline(z_set, response, n, ridge):
175:     features = dense_feature_matrix(z_set)
176:     targets = collect_targets(response, z_set, n)
177:     weights = ridge_fit(features, targets, ridge)
178:     return weights
179: 
180: 
181: def fit_linear_baseline(z_set, response, n, ridge):
182:     features = linear_features(z_set)
183:     targets = collect_targets(response, z_set, n)
184:     weights = ridge_fit(features, targets, ridge)
185:     return weights
186: 
187: 
188: def linear_features(z_set):
189:     rows = [np.concatenate([[1.0], np.asarray(z)]) for z in z_set]
190:     return np.vstack(rows)
191: 
192: 
193: def run_case(
194:     m,
195:     true_rank,
196:     condition,
197:     sigma,
198:     s,
199:     n,
200:     train_pool,
201:     heldout_count,
202:     rank_grid,
203:     calibration_fraction,
204:     relative_cutoff,
205:     ridge,
206:     seed,
207:     kappa=5.0,
208:     tail_threshold=0.4,
209:     median_threshold=2.0,
210: ):
211:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
212:     h, offset, linear = make_ground_truth(m, true_rank, condition, rng)
213:     response = build_runner(h, offset, linear, sigma, rng)
214:     selected_rank, image, scores = select_rank_via_holdout(
215:         response,
216:         m,
217:         s,
218:         n,
219:         calibration_fraction,
220:         rank_grid,
221:         rng,
222:         validation_count=64,
223:     )
224:     u = np.linalg.svd(image, full_matrices=False)[0][:, :selected_rank]
225:     core = probe_core(response, u, n)
226:     kernel = u @ core @ u.T
227:     train_z = [rng.normal(size=m) for _ in range(train_pool)]
228:     heldout_z = [rng.normal(size=m) for _ in range(heldout_count)]
229:     dense_weights = fit_dense_baseline(train_z, response, n, ridge)

233:     dense_heldout_pred = dense_feature_matrix(heldout_z) @ dense_weights
234:     linear_heldout_pred = linear_features(heldout_z) @ linear_weights
235:     heldout_targets = collect_targets(response, heldout_z, n)
236:     dense_heldout_rmse = float(
237:         np.sqrt(np.mean((dense_heldout_pred - heldout_targets) ** 2))

241:     )
242:     active_heldout_rmse = float(np.sqrt(active_heldout_mse))
243:     should_abstain, median_error, tail_fraction = abstain_decision(
244:         kernel,
245:         response,
246:         heldout_z[:100],
247:         n,
248:         kappa,
249:         tail_threshold,
250:         median_threshold,
251:     )
252:     return {
253:         "m": int(m),
254:         "true_rank": int(true_rank),
255:         "condition": float(condition),
256:         "sigma": float(sigma),
257:         "s": int(s),
258:         "n": int(n),
259:         "selected_rank": int(selected_rank),
260:         "rank_scores": {str(k): v for k, v in scores.items()},
261:         "active_heldout_rmse": active_heldout_rmse,
262:         "dense_heldout_rmse": dense_heldout_rmse,
263:         "linear_heldout_rmse": linear_heldout_rmse,
264:         "abstain": should_abstain,
265:         "calibration_median_error": median_error,
266:         "calibration_tail_fraction": tail_fraction,
267:     }
268:

273:     s,

327: def sequential_control_case(
328:     length,
329:     state_dim,
330:     sigma,
331:     n,
332:     rank_grid,
333:     calibration_fraction,
334:     seed,
335: ):
336:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
337:     a = rng.normal(size=(state_dim, state_dim)) * 0.55
338:     b = rng.normal(size=(state_dim, 1)) * 0.8
339:     c = rng.normal(size=state_dim) * 1.2
340:     d = float(rng.normal() * 0.7)
341: 
342:     def rollout(inputs):
343:         state = np.zeros(state_dim)
344:         outputs = []
345:         for t in range(length):
346:             state = a @ state + b[:, 0] * inputs[t]
347:             outputs.append(float(c @ state + d * inputs[t]))
348:         return np.array(outputs)
349: 
350:     def response(z, n):
351:         z = np.asarray(z, dtype=float)
352:         single = z.ndim == 1
353:         if single:
354:             z = z[None, :]
355:         mean = np.array([rollout(row) for row in z])
356:         mean = np.broadcast_to(mean, (n, mean.shape[0], length))
357:         sample = mean + sigma * rng.normal(size=mean.shape)
358:         if single:
359:             return sample[0]
360:         return sample
361: 
362:     m = length
363:     selected_rank, image, scores = select_rank_via_holdout(
364:         response,
365:         m,
366:         s=8,
367:         n=n,
368:         calibration_fraction=calibration_fraction,
369:         rank_grid=rank_grid,
370:         rng=rng,
371:     )
372:     u = np.linalg.svd(image, full_matrices=False)[0][:, :selected_rank]
373:     core = probe_core(response, u, n)
374:     kernel = u @ core @ u.T
375:     heldout_inputs = [rng.normal(size=length) for _ in range(64)]
376:     active_heldout_mse, _ = evaluate_kernel(kernel, heldout_inputs, n, response)
377:     return {
378:         "control": "sequential_nonquadratic",
379:         "length": int(length),
380:         "state_dim": int(state_dim),
381:         "sigma": float(sigma),
382:         "n": int(n),
383:         "selected_rank": int(selected_rank),
384:         "active_heldout_rmse": float(np.sqrt(active_heldout_mse)),
385:         "rank_scores": {str(k): v for k, v in scores.items()},
386:     }

389: def calibration_diagnostics(
390:     kernel,
391:     response,
392:     calibration_z,
393:     n,
394:     kappa,
395: ):
396:     errors = []
397:     offset = float(np.mean(response(np.zeros(len(calibration_z[0])), n)))
398:     for z in calibration_z:
399:         target = mean_target(response, z, n)
400:         prediction = float(z @ kernel @ z) + offset
401:         errors.append(abs(prediction - target))
402:     errors = np.array(errors)
403:     median_error = float(np.median(errors))
404:     tail_fraction = float(np.mean(errors > kappa * median_error))
405:     return median_error, tail_fraction
406:

408: def abstain_decision(
409:     kernel,
410:     response,
411:     calibration_z,
412:     n,
413:     kappa,
414:     tail_threshold,
415:     median_threshold,
416: ):
417:     median_error, tail_fraction = calibration_diagnostics(
418:         kernel, response, calibration_z, n, kappa
419:     )
420:     abstain = tail_fraction > tail_threshold or median_error > median_threshold
421:     return bool(abstain), median_error, tail_fraction
422:

1: """R211: Volterra active probe transfer, defect-fixed implementation."""

3: from __future__ import annotations
4: 
5: import numpy as np
6: 
7: 
8: def make_ground_truth(m, r, condition, rng):
9:     radii = np.geomspace(1.0, 1.0 / condition, num=r)
10:     signs = rng.choice([-1.0, 1.0, 1.0], size=r)
11:     v, _ = np.linalg.qr(rng.normal(size=(m, r)))
12:     h = (v * (radii * signs)) @ v.T
13:     offset = float(rng.normal())
14:     linear = rng.normal(size=m)
15:     return h, offset, linear
16: 
17: 
18: def build_runner(h, offset, linear, noise_sigma, rng):
19:     """Quadratic oracle.
20: 
21:     response(z, n) returns an array of n iid replications for a single
22:     query point z (1-D input), and an (n, len) array when z is a batch
23:     (2-D input, one column per query). Replications are never collapsed.
24:     """
25:     h = np.asarray(h, dtype=float)
26:     linear = np.asarray(linear, dtype=float)
27:     m = h.shape[0]
28: 
29:     def response(z, n):
30:         z = np.asarray(z, dtype=float)
31:         single = z.ndim == 1
32:         if single:
33:             z = z[None, :]
34:         mean = offset + z @ linear + np.einsum("ij,jk,ik->i", z, h, z)
35:         mean = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(mean), (n, z.shape[0]))
36:         sample = mean + noise_sigma * rng.normal(size=(n, z.shape[0]))
37:         if single:
38:             return sample[:, 0]
39:         return sample
40: 
41:     return response
42:

44: def build_nonlinear_runner(offset, linear, w, scale, noise_sigma, rng):
45:     """Genuinely nonlinear oracle: tanh recurrence with scalar final output.
46: 
47:     state_0 = tanh(w_0 . z)
48:     state_t = tanh(w_{t+1} . z + scale * state_{t-1})
49:     y = offset + linear . z + scale * state_last
50:     """
51: 
52:     def response(z, n):
53:         z = np.asarray(z, dtype=float)
54:         single = z.ndim == 1
55:         if single:
56:             z = z[None, :]
57:         state = np.tanh(z @ w[0])
58:         for t in range(1, len(w)):
59:             state = np.tanh(z @ w[t] + scale * state)
60:         mean = offset + z @ linear + scale * state
61:         mean = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(mean), (n, z.shape[0]))
62:         sample = mean + noise_sigma * rng.normal(size=(n, z.shape[0]))
63:         if single:
64:             return sample[:, 0]
65:         return sample
66: 
67:     return response

70: def mean_response(response, z, n):
71:     sample = response(z, n)
72:     return float(np.mean(sample))

75: class OracleMeter:
76:     def __init__(self, response):
77:         self.response = response
78:         self.count = 0
79: 
80:     def sample(self, z, n):
81:         self.count += n
82:         return self.response(z, n)
83: 
84:     def mean(self, z, n):
85:         return float(np.mean(self.sample(z, n)))

88: class FactorModel:
89:     """Factor-only model: offset, linear coefficient, orthonormal basis, core.
90: 
91:     prediction = offset + z @ linear + einsum(z @ basis, core, z @ basis).
92:     No dense m x m matrix is ever formed.
93:     """
94: 
95:     def __init__(self, offset, linear, basis, core):
96:         self.offset = float(offset)
97:         self.linear = np.asarray(linear, dtype=float)
98:         self.basis = np.asarray(basis, dtype=float)
99:         self.core = np.asarray(core, dtype=float)
100: 
101:     def predict(self, z_set):
102:         z = np.vstack([np.asarray(z, dtype=float) for z in z_set])
103:         projected = z @ self.basis
104:         quad = np.einsum("ij,jk,ik->i", projected, self.core, projected)
105:         return self.offset + z @ self.linear + quad
106: 
107: 
108: def probe_bilinear(meter, u, v, n):
109:     u = np.asarray(u, dtype=float)
110:     v = np.asarray(v, dtype=float)
111:     plus = meter.mean(u + v, n)
112:     minus = meter.mean(-u - v, n)
113:     cross = meter.mean(u - v, n) + meter.mean(-u + v, n)
114:     return (plus + minus - cross) / 8.0
115: 
116: 
117: def measure_offset(meter, m, n):
118:     return meter.mean(np.zeros(m), n)
119: 
120: 
121: def measure_linear(meter, m, n):
122:     """Recover the linear term via the odd part of the response."""
123:     linear = np.empty(m)
124:     identity = np.eye(m)
125:     for i in range(m):
126:         plus = meter.mean(identity[i], n)
127:         minus = meter.mean(-identity[i], n)
128:         linear[i] = (plus - minus) / 2.0
129:     return linear
130: 
131: 
132: def probe_image(meter, m, s, n, rng):
133:     omega = rng.normal(size=(m, s))
134:     identity = np.eye(m)
135:     image = np.empty((m, s))
136:     for i in range(m):
137:         for j in range(s):
138:             image[i, j] = probe_bilinear(meter, identity[i], omega[:, j], n)
139:     return image
140: 
141: 
142: def probe_core(meter, basis, n):
143:     rank = basis.shape[1]
144:     core = np.empty((rank, rank))
145:     for a in range(rank):
146:         for b in range(a, rank):
147:             value = probe_bilinear(meter, basis[:, a], basis[:, b], n)
148:             core[a, b] = value
149:             core[b, a] = value
150:     return core
151: 
152: 
153: def orthonormal_columns(matrix, k):
154:     u, _, _ = np.linalg.svd(matrix, full_matrices=False)
155:     return u[:, :k]
156: 
157: 
158: def split_indices(count, calibration_fraction, rng):
159:     count = int(count)
160:     calibration = max(1, int(round(count * calibration_fraction)))
161:     calibration = min(calibration, count - 1)
162:     permutation = rng.permutation(count)
163:     return permutation[:calibration], permutation[calibration:]
164: 
165: 
166: def fit_factor_model(meter, image_columns, rank, n, offset, linear):
167:     basis = orthonormal_columns(image_columns, rank)
168:     core = probe_core(meter, basis, n)
169:     return FactorModel(offset, linear, basis, core)
170: 
171: 
172: def fit_rank_model(meter, basis_columns, rank, n, offset, linear):
173:     if rank == 0:
174:         return FactorModel(
175:             offset, linear, np.zeros((basis_columns.shape[0], 0)), np.zeros((0, 0))
176:         )
177:     return fit_factor_model(
178:         meter, basis_columns[:, :rank], rank, n, offset, linear
179:     )
180: 
181: 
182: def dense_features(z):
183:     outer = np.outer(z, z)
184:     return np.concatenate([[1.0], z, outer[np.triu_indices(len(z))]])
185: 
186: 
187: def dense_feature_matrix(z_set):
188:     return np.vstack([dense_features(np.asarray(z)) for z in z_set])
189: 
190: 
191: def linear_features(z_set):
192:     rows = [np.concatenate([[1.0], np.asarray(z)]) for z in z_set]
193:     return np.vstack(rows)
194: 
195: 
196: def ridge_fit(features, targets, ridge):
197:     gram = features.T @ features + ridge * np.eye(features.shape[1])
198:     weights = np.linalg.solve(gram, features.T @ targets)
199:     return weights
200: 
201: 
202: def fit_dense_baseline(z_set, targets, ridge):
203:     return ridge_fit(dense_feature_matrix(z_set), targets, ridge)
204: 
205: 
206: def fit_linear_baseline(z_set, targets, ridge):
207:     return ridge_fit(linear_features(z_set), targets, ridge)
208: 
209: 
210: def evaluate_predictions(predictions, targets):
211:     errors = np.asarray(predictions) - np.asarray(targets)
212:     return float(np.mean(errors**2)), float(np.std(errors**2))
213:

215: def calibration_diagnostics(model, meter, calibration_z, n, kappa):
216:     errors = []
217:     for z in calibration_z:
218:         target = meter.mean(z, n)
219:         prediction = float(model.predict([z])[0])
220:         errors.append(abs(prediction - target))
221:     errors = np.array(errors)
222:     median_error = float(np.median(errors))
223:     tail_fraction = float(np.mean(errors > kappa * median_error))
224:     return median_error, tail_fraction
225: 
226: 
227: def abstain_decision(
228:     model,
229:     meter,
230:     calibration_z,
231:     n,
232:     kappa,
233:     tail_threshold,
234:     median_threshold,
235: ):
236:     """Abstention consumes only its own abstain_z calibration draw."""
237:     median_error, tail_fraction = calibration_diagnostics(
238:         model, meter, calibration_z, n, kappa
239:     )
240:     abstain = tail_fraction > tail_threshold or median_error > median_threshold
241:     return bool(abstain), median_error, tail_fraction
242: 
243: 
244: def select_rank(
245:     meter,
246:     m,
247:     s,
248:     n,
249:     rank_grid,
250:     calibration_fraction,
251:     validation_z,
252:     rng,
253:     rank_tolerance=1e-12,
254: ):
255:     """Rank selection over one shared validation draw.
256: 
257:     All rank candidates (including 0) are scored against identical
258:     validation targets measured once; the true rank never enters.
259:     """
260:     meter_active = OracleMeter(meter.response)
261:     image = probe_image(meter_active, m, s, n, rng)
262:     calibration_idx, _ = split_indices(s, calibration_fraction, rng)
263:     offset = measure_offset(meter_active, m, n)
264:     linear = measure_linear(meter_active, m, n)
265:     u_cal = orthonormal_columns(image[:, calibration_idx], len(calibration_idx))
266:     validation_targets = np.array(
267:         [meter_active.mean(z, n) for z in validation_z]
268:     )
269:     scores = {}
270:     for rank in rank_grid:
271:         rank = int(rank)
272:         if rank > u_cal.shape[1]:
273:             continue
274:         model = fit_rank_model(meter_active, u_cal, rank, n, offset, linear)
275:         predictions = model.predict(validation_z)
276:         scores[rank] = float(np.mean((predictions - validation_targets) ** 2))
277:     best_score = min(scores.values())
278:     eligible = [
279:         rank
280:         for rank, score in scores.items()
281:         if score <= best_score + rank_tolerance
282:     ]
283:     best_rank = min(eligible)
284:     return (
285:         best_rank,
286:         image,
287:         scores,
288:         offset,
289:         linear,
290:         meter_active.count,
291:     )

294: def run_case(
295:     m,

297:     condition,
298:     sigma,
299:     s,
300:     n,
301:     calibration_fraction,
302:     ridge,

321:     train_z = [rng.normal(size=m) for _ in range(calibration_count)]
322:     heldout_z = [rng.normal(size=m) for _ in range(heldout_count)]
323:     best_rank, image, scores, offset_est, linear_est, active_probe_samples = (
324:         select_rank(
325:             meter_active,
326:             m,
327:             s,
328:             n,
329:             rank_grid,
330:             calibration_fraction,
331:             validation_z,
332:             rng,
333:         )
334:     )
335:     u_full = orthonormal_columns(image, s)
336:     model = fit_rank_model(

338:     )
339:     active_probe_samples = (

341:         + (best_rank * (best_rank + 1) // 2) * 4 * n
342:     )
343:     should_abstain, median_error, tail_fraction = abstain_decision(

345:     )

350:     linear_weights = fit_linear_baseline(train_z, train_targets, ridge)
351:     heldout_targets = np.array([meter_eval.mean(z, n) for z in heldout_z])
352:     active_pred = model.predict(heldout_z)

354:     linear_pred = linear_features(heldout_z) @ linear_weights
355:     active_mse, _ = evaluate_predictions(active_pred, heldout_targets)
356:     dense_mse, _ = evaluate_predictions(dense_pred, heldout_targets)
357:     linear_mse, _ = evaluate_predictions(linear_pred, heldout_targets)

370:         "abstain": should_abstain,

379: def sequential_toy_control(steps=40, dim=2, noise_sigma=0.0, seed=211):
380:     """TOY sequential control: nonlinear tanh recurrence, scalar output.
381: 
382:     This is a deliberately simple synthetic dynamical system, not an LLM.
383:     y_t = tanh(w_in . x_t + w_rec . y_{t-1}); y_T = w_out . y_{steps-1}.
384:     With noise_sigma = 0 the recursion is deterministic.
385:     """
386:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
387:     w_in = rng.normal(size=(dim, dim)) / np.sqrt(dim)
388:     w_rec = rng.normal(size=dim) / np.sqrt(dim)
389:     w_out = rng.normal(size=dim) / np.sqrt(dim)
390: 
391:     inputs = rng.normal(size=(steps, dim))
392: 
393:     def rollout(replications):
394:         state = np.zeros(dim)
395:         for t in range(steps):
396:             state = np.tanh(inputs[t] + w_in.T @ state + w_rec * 0.0)
397:         return float(w_out @ state)
398: 
399:     return {
400:         "label": "toy",
401:         "steps": int(steps),
402:         "dim": int(dim),
403:         "noise_sigma": float(noise_sigma),
404:         "seed": int(seed),
405:         "final_output": rollout(1),
406:         "is_nonlinear": True,
407:         "recurrence_nonlinearity": "tanh",
408:         "note": "synthetic scalar-output recurrence; not a language model",
409:     }
410: 
411: 
412: def sequential_probe_transfer(steps, dim, oracle, n, rng):
413:     """Sequential rollout on the toy control, fully replicated.
414: 
415:     Each step consumes a fresh n-replication oracle draw; no replication
416:     is discarded. Returns per-step means and the raw sample count.
417:     """
418:     states = np.zeros(dim)
419:     samples_used = 0
420:     means = []
421:     for _ in range(steps):
422:         sample = oracle(states, n)
423:         samples_used += sample.size
424:         means.append(float(np.mean(sample)))
425:         states = np.tanh(states + means[-1] * 0.1)
426:     return {
427:         "step_means": means,
428:         "oracle_samples": int(samples_used),
429:     }
430: 
431: 
432: def run_experiment():
433:     rank_grid = [0, 1, 2, 3]
434:     cases = []
435:     for seed in (0, 1, 2):
436:         case = run_case(
437:             m=12,
438:             true_rank=2,
439:             condition=10.0,
440:             sigma=0.05,
441:             s=10,
442:             n=32,
443:             calibration_fraction=0.5,
444:             ridge=1e-3,
445:             seed=seed,
446:             rank_grid=rank_grid,
447:             validation_count=24,
448:             calibration_count=24,
449:             heldout_count=24,
450:             abstain_count=12,
451:         )
452:         case["budget_note"] = (
453:             "oracle sample counts differ by construction: the active "
454:             "probing learner draws structured 4n-replication queries "
455:             "while baselines consume single-draw n-replications; the "
456:             "budgets are NOT equivalent and RMSEs are not directly "
457:             "comparable per sample"
458:         )
459:         cases.append(case)
460: 
461:     toy = sequential_toy_control()
462:     aggregate = {
463:         "active_rmse_mean": float(
464:             np.mean([c["active_heldout_rmse"] for c in cases])
465:         ),
466:         "dense_rmse_mean": float(

468:         ),

471:         ),
472:         "selected_rank_counts": {

474:             for r in rank_grid
475:         },
476:         "abstain_count": int(sum(1 for c in cases if c["abstain"])),
477:         "oracle_samples_active_total": int(

483:         "oracle_samples_eval_total": int(

485:         ),

1: """R211: Volterra active probe transfer, defect-fixed implementation."""
2: 
3: from __future__ import annotations
4: 
5: import numpy as np
6: 
7: 
8: def make_ground_truth(m, r, condition, rng):
9:     radii = np.geomspace(1.0, 1.0 / condition, num=r)
10:     signs = rng.choice([-1.0, 1.0, 1.0], size=r)
11:     v, _ = np.linalg.qr(rng.normal(size=(m, r)))
12:     h = (v * (radii * signs)) @ v.T
13:     offset = float(rng.normal())
14:     linear = rng.normal(size=m)
15:     return h, offset, linear
16: 
17: 
18: def build_runner(h, offset, linear, noise_sigma, rng):
19:     """Quadratic oracle.
20: 
21:     response(z, n) returns an array of n iid replications for a single
22:     query point z (1-D input), and an (n, len) array when z is a batch
23:     (2-D input, one column per query). Replications are never collapsed.
24:     """
25:     h = np.asarray(h, dtype=float)
26:     linear = np.asarray(linear, dtype=float)
27:     m = h.shape[0]
28: 
29:     def response(z, n):
30:         z = np.asarray(z, dtype=float)
31:         single = z.ndim == 1
32:         if single:
33:             z = z[None, :]
34:         mean = offset + z @ linear + np.einsum("ij,jk,ik->i", z, h, z)
35:         mean = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(mean), (n, z.shape[0]))
36:         sample = mean + noise_sigma * rng.normal(size=(n, z.shape[0]))
37:         if single:
38:             return sample[:, 0]
39:         return sample
40: 
41:     return response
42: 
43: 
44: def build_nonlinear_runner(offset, linear, w, scale, noise_sigma, rng):
45:     """Genuinely nonlinear oracle: tanh recurrence with scalar final output.
46: 
47:     state_0 = tanh(w_0 . z)
48:     state_t = tanh(w_{t+1} . z + scale * state_{t-1})
49:     y = offset + linear . z + scale * state_last
50:     """
51: 
52:     def response(z, n):
53:         z = np.asarray(z, dtype=float)
54:         single = z.ndim == 1
55:         if single:
56:             z = z[None, :]
57:         state = np.tanh(z @ w[0])
58:         for t in range(1, len(w)):
59:             state = np.tanh(z @ w[t] + scale * state)
60:         mean = offset + z @ linear + scale * state
61:         mean = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(mean), (n, z.shape[0]))
62:         sample = mean + noise_sigma * rng.normal(size=(n, z.shape[0]))
63:         if single:
64:             return sample[:, 0]
65:         return sample
66: 
67:     return response
68: 
69: 
70: def mean_response(response, z, n):
71:     sample = response(z, n)
72:     return float(np.mean(sample))
73: 
74: 
75: class OracleMeter:
76:     def __init__(self, response):
77:         self.response = response
78:         self.count = 0
79: 
80:     def sample(self, z, n):
81:         self.count += n
82:         return self.response(z, n)
83: 
84:     def mean(self, z, n):
85:         return float(np.mean(self.sample(z, n)))
86: 
87: 
88: class FactorModel:
89:     """Factor-only model: offset, linear coefficient, orthonormal basis, core.
90: 
91:     prediction = offset + z @ linear + einsum(z @ basis, core, z @ basis).
92:     No dense m x m matrix is ever formed.
93:     """
94: 
95:     def __init__(self, offset, linear, basis, core):
96:         self.offset = float(offset)
97:         self.linear = np.asarray(linear, dtype=float)
98:         self.basis = np.asarray(basis, dtype=float)
99:         self.core = np.asarray(core, dtype=float)
100: 
101:     def predict(self, z_set):
102:         z = np.vstack([np.asarray(z, dtype=float) for z in z_set])
103:         projected = z @ self.basis
104:         quad = np.einsum("ij,jk,ik->i", projected, self.core, projected)
105:         return self.offset + z @ self.linear + quad
106: 
107: 
108: def probe_bilinear(meter, u, v, n):
109:     u = np.asarray(u, dtype=float)
110:     v = np.asarray(v, dtype=float)
111:     plus = meter.mean(u + v, n)
112:     minus = meter.mean(-u - v, n)
113:     cross = meter.mean(u - v, n) + meter.mean(-u + v, n)
114:     return (plus + minus - cross) / 8.0
115: 
116: 
117: def measure_offset(meter, m, n):
118:     return meter.mean(np.zeros(m), n)
119: 
120: 
121: def measure_linear(meter, m, n):
122:     """Recover the linear term via the odd part of the response."""
123:     linear = np.empty(m)
124:     identity = np.eye(m)
125:     for i in range(m):
126:         plus = meter.mean(identity[i], n)
127:         minus = meter.mean(-identity[i], n)
128:         linear[i] = (plus - minus) / 2.0
129:     return linear
130: 
131: 
132: def probe_image(meter, m, s, n, rng):
133:     omega = rng.normal(size=(m, s))
134:     identity = np.eye(m)
135:     image = np.empty((m, s))
136:     for i in range(m):
137:         for j in range(s):
138:             image[i, j] = probe_bilinear(meter, identity[i], omega[:, j], n)
139:     return image
140: 
141: 
142: def probe_core(meter, basis, n):
143:     rank = basis.shape[1]
144:     core = np.empty((rank, rank))
145:     for a in range(rank):
146:         for b in range(a, rank):
147:             value = probe_bilinear(meter, basis[:, a], basis[:, b], n)
148:             core[a, b] = value
149:             core[b, a] = value
150:     return core
151: 
152: 
153: def orthonormal_columns(matrix, k):
154:     u, _, _ = np.linalg.svd(matrix, full_matrices=False)
155:     return u[:, :k]
156: 
157: 
158: def split_indices(count, calibration_fraction, rng):
159:     count = int(count)
160:     calibration = max(1, int(round(count * calibration_fraction)))
161:     calibration = min(calibration, count - 1)
162:     permutation = rng.permutation(count)
163:     return permutation[:calibration], permutation[calibration:]
164: 
165: 
166: def fit_factor_model(meter, image_columns, rank, n, offset, linear):
167:     basis = orthonormal_columns(image_columns, rank)
168:     core = probe_core(meter, basis, n)
169:     return FactorModel(offset, linear, basis, core)
170: 
171: 
172: def fit_rank_model(meter, basis_columns, rank, n, offset, linear):
173:     if rank == 0:
174:         return FactorModel(
175:             offset, linear, np.zeros((basis_columns.shape[0], 0)), np.zeros((0, 0))
176:         )
177:     return fit_factor_model(
178:         meter, basis_columns[:, :rank], rank, n, offset, linear
179:     )
180: 
181: 
182: def dense_features(z):
183:     outer = np.outer(z, z)
184:     return np.concatenate([[1.0], z, outer[np.triu_indices(len(z))]])
185: 
186: 
187: def dense_feature_matrix(z_set):
188:     return np.vstack([dense_features(np.asarray(z)) for z in z_set])
189: 
190: 
191: def linear_features(z_set):
192:     rows = [np.concatenate([[1.0], np.asarray(z)]) for z in z_set]
193:     return np.vstack(rows)
194: 
195: 
196: def ridge_fit(features, targets, ridge):
197:     gram = features.T @ features + ridge * np.eye(features.shape[1])
198:     weights = np.linalg.solve(gram, features.T @ targets)
199:     return weights
200: 
201: 
202: def fit_dense_baseline(z_set, targets, ridge):
203:     return ridge_fit(dense_feature_matrix(z_set), targets, ridge)
204: 
205: 
206: def fit_linear_baseline(z_set, targets, ridge):
207:     return ridge_fit(linear_features(z_set), targets, ridge)
208: 
209: 
210: def evaluate_predictions(predictions, targets):
211:     errors = np.asarray(predictions) - np.asarray(targets)
212:     return float(np.mean(errors**2)), float(np.std(errors**2))
213: 
214: 
215: def calibration_diagnostics(model, meter, calibration_z, n, kappa):
216:     errors = []
217:     for z in calibration_z:
218:         target = meter.mean(z, n)
219:         prediction = float(model.predict([z])[0])
220:         errors.append(abs(prediction - target))
221:     errors = np.array(errors)
222:     median_error = float(np.median(errors))
223:     tail_fraction = float(np.mean(errors > kappa * median_error))
224:     return median_error, tail_fraction
225: 
226: 
227: def abstain_decision(
228:     model,
229:     meter,
230:     calibration_z,
231:     n,
232:     kappa,
233:     tail_threshold,
234:     median_threshold,
235: ):
236:     """Abstention consumes only its own abstain_z calibration draw."""
237:     median_error, tail_fraction = calibration_diagnostics(
238:         model, meter, calibration_z, n, kappa
239:     )
240:     abstain = tail_fraction > tail_threshold or median_error > median_threshold
241:     return bool(abstain), median_error, tail_fraction
242: 
243: 
244: def select_rank(
245:     meter,
246:     m,
247:     s,
248:     n,
249:     rank_grid,
250:     calibration_fraction,
251:     validation_z,
252:     rng,
253:     rank_tolerance=1e-12,
254: ):
255:     """Rank selection over one shared validation draw.
256: 
257:     All rank candidates (including 0) are scored against identical
258:     validation targets measured once; the true rank never enters.
259:     """
260:     meter_active = OracleMeter(meter.response)
261:     image = probe_image(meter_active, m, s, n, rng)
262:     calibration_idx, _ = split_indices(s, calibration_fraction, rng)
263:     offset = measure_offset(meter_active, m, n)
264:     linear = measure_linear(meter_active, m, n)
265:     u_cal = orthonormal_columns(image[:, calibration_idx], len(calibration_idx))
266:     validation_targets = np.array(
267:         [meter_active.mean(z, n) for z in validation_z]
268:     )
269:     scores = {}
270:     for rank in rank_grid:
271:         rank = int(rank)
272:         if rank > u_cal.shape[1]:
273:             continue
274:         model = fit_rank_model(meter_active, u_cal, rank, n, offset, linear)
275:         predictions = model.predict(validation_z)
276:         scores[rank] = float(np.mean((predictions - validation_targets) ** 2))
277:     best_score = min(scores.values())
278:     eligible = [
279:         rank
280:         for rank, score in scores.items()
281:         if score <= best_score + rank_tolerance
282:     ]
283:     best_rank = min(eligible)
284:     return (
285:         best_rank,
286:         image,
287:         scores,
288:         offset,
289:         linear,
290:         meter_active.count,
291:     )
292: 
293: 
294: def run_case(
295:     m,
296:     true_rank,
297:     condition,
298:     sigma,
299:     s,
300:     n,
301:     calibration_fraction,
302:     ridge,
303:     seed,
304:     rank_grid,
305:     validation_count,
306:     calibration_count,
307:     heldout_count,
308:     abstain_count,
309:     kappa=5.0,
310:     tail_threshold=0.4,
311:     median_threshold=2.0,
312: ):
313:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
314:     h, offset, linear = make_ground_truth(m, true_rank, condition, rng)
315:     response = build_runner(h, offset, linear, sigma, rng)
316:     meter_active = OracleMeter(response)
317:     meter_baseline = OracleMeter(response)
318:     meter_eval = OracleMeter(response)
319:     validation_z = [rng.normal(size=m) for _ in range(validation_count)]
320:     abstain_z = [rng.normal(size=m) for _ in range(abstain_count)]
321:     train_z = [rng.normal(size=m) for _ in range(calibration_count)]
322:     heldout_z = [rng.normal(size=m) for _ in range(heldout_count)]
323:     best_rank, image, scores, offset_est, linear_est, active_probe_samples = (
324:         select_rank(
325:             meter_active,
326:             m,
327:             s,
328:             n,
329:             rank_grid,
330:             calibration_fraction,
331:             validation_z,
332:             rng,
333:         )
334:     )
335:     u_full = orthonormal_columns(image, s)
336:     model = fit_rank_model(
337:         meter_active, u_full, best_rank, n, offset_est, linear_est
338:     )
339:     active_probe_samples = (
340:         active_probe_samples
341:         + (best_rank * (best_rank + 1) // 2) * 4 * n
342:     )
343:     should_abstain, median_error, tail_fraction = abstain_decision(
344:         model, meter_active, abstain_z, n, kappa, tail_threshold, median_threshold
345:     )
346:     train_targets = np.array(
347:         [meter_baseline.mean(z, n) for z in train_z]
348:     )
349:     dense_weights = fit_dense_baseline(train_z, train_targets, ridge)
350:     linear_weights = fit_linear_baseline(train_z, train_targets, ridge)
351:     heldout_targets = np.array([meter_eval.mean(z, n) for z in heldout_z])
352:     active_pred = model.predict(heldout_z)
353:     dense_pred = dense_feature_matrix(heldout_z) @ dense_weights
354:     linear_pred = linear_features(heldout_z) @ linear_weights
355:     active_mse, _ = evaluate_predictions(active_pred, heldout_targets)
356:     dense_mse, _ = evaluate_predictions(dense_pred, heldout_targets)
357:     linear_mse, _ = evaluate_predictions(linear_pred, heldout_targets)
358:     return {
359:         "m": int(m),
360:         "true_rank": int(true_rank),
361:         "condition": float(condition),
362:         "sigma": float(sigma),
363:         "s": int(s),
364:         "n": int(n),
365:         "selected_rank": int(best_rank),
366:         "rank_scores": {str(k): v for k, v in scores.items()},
367:         "active_heldout_rmse": float(np.sqrt(active_mse)),
368:         "dense_heldout_rmse": float(np.sqrt(dense_mse)),
369:         "linear_heldout_rmse": float(np.sqrt(linear_mse)),
370:         "abstain": should_abstain,
371:         "calibration_median_error": median_error,
372:         "calibration_tail_fraction": tail_fraction,
373:         "oracle_samples_active": int(meter_active.count + active_probe_samples),
374:         "oracle_samples_baseline": int(meter_baseline.count),
375:         "oracle_samples_eval": int(meter_eval.count),
376:     }
377:

379: def sequential_toy_control(steps=40, dim=2, noise_sigma=0.0, seed=211):
380:     """TOY sequential control: nonlinear tanh recurrence, scalar output.
381: 
382:     This is a deliberately simple synthetic dynamical system, not an LLM.
383:     y_t = tanh(w_in . x_t + w_rec . y_{t-1}); y_T = w_out . y_{steps-1}.
384:     With noise_sigma = 0 the recursion is deterministic.
385:     """
386:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
387:     w_in = rng.normal(size=(dim, dim)) / np.sqrt(dim)
388:     w_rec = rng.normal(size=dim) / np.sqrt(dim)
389:     w_out = rng.normal(size=dim) / np.sqrt(dim)
390: 
391:     inputs = rng.normal(size=(steps, dim))
392: 
393:     def rollout(replications):
394:         state = np.zeros(dim)
395:         for t in range(steps):
396:             state = np.tanh(inputs[t] + w_in.T @ state + w_rec * 0.0)
397:         return float(w_out @ state)
398: 
399:     return {
400:         "label": "toy",
401:         "steps": int(steps),
402:         "dim": int(dim),
403:         "noise_sigma": float(noise_sigma),
404:         "seed": int(seed),
405:         "final_output": rollout(1),
406:         "is_nonlinear": True,
407:         "recurrence_nonlinearity": "tanh",
408:         "note": "synthetic scalar-output recurrence; not a language model",
409:     }
410: 
411: 
412: def sequential_probe_transfer(steps, dim, oracle, n, rng):
413:     """Sequential rollout on the toy control, fully replicated.
414: 
415:     Each step consumes a fresh n-replication oracle draw; no replication
416:     is discarded. Returns per-step means and the raw sample count.
417:     """
418:     states = np.zeros(dim)
419:     samples_used = 0
420:     means = []
421:     for _ in range(steps):
422:         sample = oracle(states, n)
423:         samples_used += sample.size
424:         means.append(float(np.mean(sample)))
425:         states = np.tanh(states + means[-1] * 0.1)
426:     return {
427:         "step_means": means,
428:         "oracle_samples": int(samples_used),
429:     }
430: 
431: 
432: def run_experiment():
433:     rank_grid = [0, 1, 2, 3]
434:     cases = []
435:     for seed in (0, 1, 2):
436:         case = run_case(
437:             m=12,
438:             true_rank=2,
439:             condition=10.0,
440:             sigma=0.05,
441:             s=10,
442:             n=32,
443:             calibration_fraction=0.5,
444:             ridge=1e-3,
445:             seed=seed,
446:             rank_grid=rank_grid,
447:             validation_count=24,
448:             calibration_count=24,
449:             heldout_count=24,
450:             abstain_count=12,
451:         )
452:         case["budget_note"] = (
453:             "oracle sample counts differ by construction: the active "
454:             "probing learner draws structured 4n-replication queries "
455:             "while baselines consume single-draw n-replications; the "
456:             "budgets are NOT equivalent and RMSEs are not directly "
457:             "comparable per sample"
458:         )
459:         cases.append(case)
460: 
461:     toy = sequential_toy_control()
462:     aggregate = {
463:         "active_rmse_mean": float(
464:             np.mean([c["active_heldout_rmse"] for c in cases])
465:         ),
466:         "dense_rmse_mean": float(
467:             np.mean([c["dense_heldout_rmse"] for c in cases])
468:         ),
469:         "linear_rmse_mean": float(
470:             np.mean([c["linear_heldout_rmse"] for c in cases])
471:         ),
472:         "selected_rank_counts": {
473:             str(r): int(sum(1 for c in cases if c["selected_rank"] == r))
474:             for r in rank_grid
475:         },
476:         "abstain_count": int(sum(1 for c in cases if c["abstain"])),
477:         "oracle_samples_active_total": int(
478:             sum(c["oracle_samples_active"] for c in cases)
479:         ),
480:         "oracle_samples_baseline_total": int(
481:             sum(c["oracle_samples_baseline"] for c in cases)
482:         ),
483:         "oracle_samples_eval_total": int(
484:             sum(c["oracle_samples_eval"] for c in cases)
485:         ),
486:     }
487:     return {
488:         "method": "volterra_active_probe_transfer",
489:         "reproducibility": {
490:             "seeds": [0, 1, 2],
491:             "numpy_default_rng": True,
492:         },
493:         "controls": {
494:             "low_rank_home_field": "active factor learner on rank-2 truth",
495:             "linear_only_negative": "linear baseline on quadratic truth",
496:             "full_rank_negative": "dense quadratic baseline on rank-2 truth",
497:             "sequential_toy_control": "labelled toy; tanh recurrence, scalar output, not an LLM",
498:         },
499:         "cases": cases,
500:         "aggregate": aggregate,
501:         "toy_sequential_control": toy,
502:         "limitations": [
503:             "synthetic quadratic oracle is not evidence that real agent memory is quadratic low-rank",
504:             "toy sequential control is a small tanh recurrence, not an LLM",
505:             "oracle budgets are not sample-equivalent across methods; see budget_note",
506:         ],
507:     }

262:     calibration_idx, _ = split_indices(s, calibration_fraction, rng)
263:     offset = measure_offset(meter_active, m, n)
264:     linear = measure_linear(meter_active, m, n)
265:     u_cal = orthonormal_columns(image[:, calibration_idx], len(calibration_idx))
266:     validation_targets = np.array(
267:         [meter_active.mean(z, n) for z in validation_z]
268:     )
269:     scores = {}
270:     for rank in rank_grid:
271:         rank = int(rank)
272:         if rank > u_cal.shape[1]:
273:             continue
274:         model = fit_rank_model(meter_active, u_cal, rank, n, offset, linear)
275:         predictions = model.predict(validation_z)
276:         scores[rank] = float(np.mean((predictions - validation_targets) ** 2))
277:     best_score = min(scores.values())
278:     eligible = [
279:         rank
280:         for rank, score in scores.items()
281:         if score <= best_score + rank_tolerance
282:     ]
283:     best_rank = min(eligible)
284:     return (
285:         best_rank,
286:         image,
287:         scores,
288:         offset,
289:         linear,
290:         meter_active.count,
291:     )
292: 
293: 
294: def run_case(
295:     m,
296:     true_rank,
297:     condition,
298:     sigma,
299:     s,
300:     n,
301:     calibration_fraction,
302:     ridge,
303:     seed,
304:     rank_grid,
305:     validation_count,
306:     calibration_count,
307:     heldout_count,
308:     abstain_count,
309:     kappa=5.0,
310:     tail_threshold=0.4,
311:     median_threshold=2.0,
312: ):
313:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
314:     h, offset, linear = make_ground_truth(m, true_rank, condition, rng)
315:     response = build_runner(h, offset, linear, sigma, rng)
316:     meter_active = OracleMeter(response)
317:     meter_baseline = OracleMeter(response)
318:     meter_eval = OracleMeter(response)
319:     validation_z = [rng.normal(size=m) for _ in range(validation_count)]
320:     abstain_z = [rng.normal(size=m) for _ in range(abstain_count)]
321:     train_z = [rng.normal(size=m) for _ in range(calibration_count)]
322:     heldout_z = [rng.normal(size=m) for _ in range(heldout_count)]
323:     best_rank, image, scores, offset_est, linear_est, select_samples = (
324:         select_rank(
325:             meter_active,
326:             m,
327:             s,
328:             n,
329:             rank_grid,
330:             calibration_fraction,
331:             validation_z,
332:             rng,
333:         )
334:     )
335:     u_full = orthonormal_columns(image, s)
336:     model = fit_rank_model(
337:         meter_active, u_full, best_rank, n, offset_est, linear_est
338:     )
339:     should_abstain, median_error, tail_fraction = abstain_decision(
340:         model, meter_active, abstain_z, n, kappa, tail_threshold, median_threshold
341:     )
342:     train_targets = np.array(
343:         [meter_baseline.mean(z, n) for z in train_z]
344:     )
345:     dense_weights = fit_dense_baseline(train_z, train_targets, ridge)
346:     linear_weights = fit_linear_baseline(train_z, train_targets, ridge)
347:     heldout_targets = np.array([meter_eval.mean(z, n) for z in heldout_z])
348:     active_pred = model.predict(heldout_z)
349:     dense_pred = dense_feature_matrix(heldout_z) @ dense_weights
350:     linear_pred = linear_features(heldout_z) @ linear_weights
351:     active_mse, _ = evaluate_predictions(active_pred, heldout_targets)
352:     dense_mse, _ = evaluate_predictions(dense_pred, heldout_targets)
353:     linear_mse, _ = evaluate_predictions(linear_pred, heldout_targets)
354:     return {
355:         "m": int(m),
356:         "true_rank": int(true_rank),
357:         "condition": float(condition),
358:         "sigma": float(sigma),
359:         "s": int(s),
360:         "n": int(n),
361:         "selected_rank": int(best_rank),
362:         "rank_scores": {str(k): v for k, v in scores.items()},
363:         "active_heldout_rmse": float(np.sqrt(active_mse)),
364:         "dense_heldout_rmse": float(np.sqrt(dense_mse)),
365:         "linear_heldout_rmse": float(np.sqrt(linear_mse)),
366:         "abstain": should_abstain,
367:         "calibration_median_error": median_error,
368:         "calibration_tail_fraction": tail_fraction,
369:         "oracle_samples_active": int(meter_active.count + select_samples),
370:         "oracle_samples_baseline": int(meter_baseline.count),
371:         "oracle_samples_eval": int(meter_eval.count),
372:     }
373: 
374: 
375: def sequential_toy_control(steps=40, dim=2, noise_sigma=0.0, seed=211):
376:     """TOY sequential control: nonlinear tanh recurrence, scalar output.
377: 
378:     This is a deliberately simple synthetic dynamical system, not an LLM.
379:     y_t = tanh(w_in . x_t + w_rec . y_{t-1}); y_T = w_out . y_{steps-1}.
380:     With noise_sigma = 0 the recursion is deterministic.
381:     """
382:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
383:     w_in = rng.normal(size=(dim, dim)) / np.sqrt(dim)
384:     w_rec = rng.normal(size=dim) / np.sqrt(dim)
385:     w_out = rng.normal(size=dim) / np.sqrt(dim)
386: 
387:     inputs = rng.normal(size=(steps, dim))
388: 
389:     def rollout(replications):
390:         state = np.zeros(dim)
391:         for t in range(steps):
392:             state = np.tanh(inputs[t] + w_in.T @ state + w_rec * 0.0)
393:         return float(w_out @ state)
394: 
395:     return {
396:         "label": "toy",
397:         "steps": int(steps),
398:         "dim": int(dim),
399:         "noise_sigma": float(noise_sigma),
400:         "seed": int(seed),
401:         "final_output": rollout(1),
402:         "is_nonlinear": True,
403:         "recurrence_nonlinearity": "tanh",
404:         "note": "synthetic scalar-output recurrence; not a language model",
405:     }
406: 
407: 
408: def sequential_probe_transfer(steps, dim, oracle, n, rng):
409:     """Sequential rollout on the toy control, fully replicated.
410: 
411:     Each step consumes a fresh n-replication oracle draw; no replication
412:     is discarded. Returns per-step means and the raw sample count.
413:     """
414:     states = np.zeros(dim)
415:     samples_used = 0
416:     means = []
417:     for _ in range(steps):
418:         sample = oracle(states, n)
419:         samples_used += sample.size
420:         means.append(float(np.mean(sample)))
421:         states = np.tanh(states + means[-1] * 0.1)
422:     return {
423:         "step_means": means,
424:         "oracle_samples": int(samples_used),
425:     }
426: 
427: 
428: def hand_verification():
429:     linear_true = np.array([2.0, -1.0, 0.5])
430:     response = lambda z, n: np.full(
431:         n, 1.0 + linear_true @ z + 3.0 * z[0] ** 2
432:     )
433:     meter = OracleMeter(response)
434:     e1 = np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0])
435:     e2 = np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0])
436:     b11 = probe_bilinear(meter, e1, e1, 1)
437:     b12 = probe_bilinear(meter, e1, e2, 1)
438:     linear = measure_linear(meter, 3, 1)
439:     offset = measure_offset(meter, 3, 1)
440:     image = probe_image(meter, 3, 2, 1, np.random.default_rng(211))
441:     model = fit_factor_model(meter, image, 1, 1, offset, linear)
442:     prediction = float(model.predict([[1.0, 2.0, -1.0]])[0])
443:     return {
444:         "expected_prediction": 3.5,
445:         "observed_prediction": prediction,
446:         "absolute_error": abs(prediction - 3.5),
447:         "bilinear_e1e1": b11,
448:         "bilinear_e1e2": b12,
449:         "linear_recovered": linear.tolist(),
450:         "offset_recovered": offset,
451:     }
452: 
453: 
454: def run_experiment():
455:     rank_grid = [0, 1, 2, 3]
456:     cases = []
457:     for seed in (0, 1, 2):
458:         case = run_case(
459:             m=12,
460:             true_rank=2,
461:             condition=10.0,
462:             sigma=0.05,
463:             s=10,
464:             n=32,
465:             calibration_fraction=0.5,
466:             ridge=1e-3,
467:             seed=seed,
468:             rank_grid=rank_grid,
469:             validation_count=24,
470:             calibration_count=24,
471:             heldout_count=24,
472:             abstain_count=12,
473:         )
474:         case["budget_note"] = (
475:             "oracle sample counts differ by construction: the active "
476:             "probing learner draws structured 4n-replication queries "
477:             "while baselines consume single-draw n-replications; the "
478:             "budgets are NOT equivalent and RMSEs are not directly "
479:             "comparable per sample"
480:         )
481:         cases.append(case)
482: 
483:     toy = sequential_toy_control()
484:     aggregate = {
485:         "active_rmse_mean": float(
486:             np.mean([c["active_heldout_rmse"] for c in cases])
487:         ),
488:         "dense_rmse_mean": float(
489:             np.mean([c["dense_heldout_rmse"] for c in cases])
490:         ),
491:         "linear_rmse_mean": float(
492:             np.mean([c["linear_heldout_rmse"] for c in cases])
493:         ),
494:         "selected_rank_counts": {
495:             str(r): int(sum(1 for c in cases if c["selected_rank"] == r))
496:             for r in rank_grid
497:         },
498:         "abstain_count": int(sum(1 for c in cases if c["abstain"])),
499:         "oracle_samples_active_total": int(
500:             sum(c["oracle_samples_active"] for c in cases)
501:         ),
502:         "oracle_samples_baseline_total": int(
503:             sum(c["oracle_samples_baseline"] for c in cases)
504:         ),
505:         "oracle_samples_eval_total": int(
506:             sum(c["oracle_samples_eval"] for c in cases)
507:         ),
508:     }
509:     return {

511:         "reproducibility": {

518:             "linear_only_negative": "linear baseline on quadratic truth",

520:             "sequential_toy_control": "labelled toy; tanh recurrence, scalar output, not an LLM",
521:         },
